summary: The LLM settings workflow loads compact provider status first, then lazily fetches per-provider model catalogs for the specific selection surface in use.
trigger: A user opens the LLM settings modal and selects, expands, searches, saves, tests, or activates an LLM provider/model.

inputs.name: provider_id
inputs.source: Quick connect provider select, active provider select, or advanced provider row

steps.action: Load provider status through /api/llm/providers, which proxies bridge /providers without include_models.
steps.success: Provider cards and selects render with status, default_model, and model_count while model arrays are empty.
steps.failure: The existing settings error message is shown and no credential operation is attempted.

steps.action: When the quick-connect or active provider changes, call getProviderModels(providerId) unless cached.
steps.success: ModelSelect receives the provider's model list and fuzzy search works immediately after loading.
steps.failure: A field warning is shown, an empty cache entry is stored, and manual text entry remains enabled.

steps.action: When an advanced provider row expands or its chips are expanded, call getProviderModels(providerId) unless cached.
steps.success: The row can show up to 10 chips first, then the full list inside a bounded scroll area.
steps.failure: The row displays the lazy-load warning and still allows manual default model entry.

steps.action: Filter ModelSelect options locally by lowercased id/name substring with exact/prefix scores ahead of other matches.
steps.success: Queries such as claude match model IDs like anthropic/claude-3.5-sonnet and keyboard selection works.
steps.failure: No result message is shown while the typed model ID remains in the input for manual use.

steps.action: Save, test, quick-connect, or activate the model exactly through the existing provider APIs.
steps.success: Existing credential and active model behavior is preserved without echoing secrets.
steps.failure: Existing readable errors and toast messages report the failed operation.

idempotency: The model cache is keyed by provider ID and each provider is fetched at most once per modal lifetime unless the modal is recreated. Save/test/activate calls remain user-triggered.
retries: Lazy model fetch has no hidden retry loop. Users can change provider, reopen settings, or type a model ID manually after failure.
credentials: API keys remain handled by existing quick-connect and provider save endpoints
OAuth credentials remain handled by existing OAuth endpoints
Model catalog loading does not require or expose credentials
observability: Loading state is visible through ModelSelect spinner/placeholder
Lazy-load failure is visible through field warning text
Bridge server tests capture compact and full provider behavior
Payload probe records response byte counts
manual_override: Users can always type an arbitrary model ID into ModelSelect and submit through the existing flows.

state_model.exit: User selects or expands a provider
Models are cached or failure is cached
state_model.on_error: Set an empty cache entry and modelLoadErrors[providerId]

state_model.exit: ModelSelect filters locally or chips render
state_model.on_error: No remote call occurs in this state

state_model.entry: User types an ID while no option exists or loading failed
state_model.exit: Existing save/test/activate flow receives the typed ID

compensation: No persistent model cache is written. Closing and reopening the modal clears all lazy cache, loading, error, and chip expansion state.
concurrency: Concurrent duplicate fetches are prevented by the modelLoading set; independent providers can load independently.
timeout_policy: Fetch timeout behavior is inherited from browser fetch and the FastAPI/bridge request path; the UI does not spin or poll.
